analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR BRAZIL + M&A 5 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 closed +66bps at 7,773 with a $5Bn market-on-close imbalance to SELL. NDX +87bps at 31,076, R2K +73bps at 2,853, Dow +18bps at 51,267.
Volume was muted: 16.827bn shares traded across US exchanges vs a YTD daily average of 18.647bn. TMT volumes were down 10-20% vs 10-day averages.

Brazil was the topical market after election results (Flávio Bolsonaro 47.0%, Lula 45.2%), described as substantially better for the market than expected. EWZ rose 13%. The desk saw broad hedge fund demand vs long-only supply in high beta pockets and thinks macro shorts were likely squeezed.

Merger Monday: Schneider Electric announced it will acquire PTX for $22.6bn and C.H. Robinson announced a deal to acquire RXO for $5.8bn. After the market, an FT headline said McKesson and CD&R are near a $5bn-plus deal to buy infusion services provider OPCH, which traded +20% after hours.
The GS floor rated activity a 4 on a 1-10 scale. Flow skewed benign, with long-onlys slight net sellers driven by macro products and hedge funds slight net buyers driven by tech.

The desk sees no real signs of chasing. US L/S net leverage is at its lowest since Apr '25 and approaching five-year lows in the 2nd percentile, so a continued index move higher would force investors to buy.

Derivatives: early flow was dominated by a chase for upside in short-dated EWZ calls plus monetization of existing positions. US indices closed higher with spot up, vol up across the board. Skew was crushed, especially in short-dated S&P.
The vol desk still sees room for further upside and likes owning QQQ optionality heading into earnings. It is constructive on semis into earnings and sees upside as attractive.
The S&P implied move for the rest of the week is 90bps.
